modules.title: AI & GenAI in Life Sciences
learning_objectives: Identify the key stages of the Life Sciences value chain and explain how AI is reshaping each stage
Describe the regulatory and data governance constraints that define how AI and ML solutions must be designed and deployed in pharma and biotech contexts

units.title: The Life Sciences Value Chain & AI's Role
learning_objectives: Identify the core phases of drug development — from target identification through post-market surveillance — and map current GenAI and ML use cases to each phase
Explain why Life Sciences AI applications differ from general enterprise AI in terms of data sensitivity, regulatory scrutiny, and validation requirements

units.title: Regulatory Landscape & Data Governance for AI in Pharma
learning_objectives: Describe key regulatory frameworks governing AI use in Life Sciences (FDA guidance on AI/ML-based software, GxP data integrity, ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice) and their implications for ML engineers
Distinguish between compliant and non-compliant AI deployment patterns in a clinical or regulatory context

modules.title: Applying GenAI in Life Sciences Workflows
learning_objectives: Apply GenAI tools (Claude, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT) to accelerate common ML engineering tasks within Life Sciences workflows — including clinical data summarisation, documentation drafting, and code review
Demonstrate effective prompt engineering techniques tailored to pharma and biotech contexts, evaluating AI outputs for accuracy, bias, and regulatory appropriateness
Identify agentic AI patterns relevant to Life Sciences engagements and explain how they can be applied to automate repetitive analytical or reporting tasks

units.title: GenAI Tools for ML Engineers in Life Sciences
learning_objectives: Apply GenAI productivity tools (Claude, Copilot, Gemini) to real ML engineering tasks in LS settings — such as drafting technical documentation, summarising trial protocols, and reviewing analysis code
Evaluate GenAI outputs for fitness-for-purpose in regulated Life Sciences environments, identifying hallucination risks and compliance considerations

units.title: Prompt Engineering & Agentic AI Patterns in Pharma Contexts
learning_objectives: Construct effective prompts for domain-specific Life Sciences tasks — including adverse event summarisation, regulatory document drafting, and clinical data interpretation
Identify agentic AI design patterns (tool-use agents, multi-step reasoning chains) and describe how they apply to automating LS analytical workflows without introducing unacceptable regulatory risk

modules.title: Delivering AI Outcomes for Life Sciences Clients
learning_objectives: Define measurable delivery outcomes for AI/ML initiatives in Life Sciences engagements — grounded in domain-relevant KPIs such as trial cycle time reduction, submission readiness, and data quality SLAs
Apply GenAI tools to monitor delivery progress, identify risks early, and communicate outcome status clearly to Life Sciences stakeholders
Evaluate the impact of an AI/ML engagement against pre-defined client outcomes, using domain-specific evidence to demonstrate value delivered

units.title: Defining & Measuring AI Outcomes in Life Sciences Engagements
learning_objectives: Construct a measurable outcome framework for an AI/ML project in a pharma or biotech context, mapping deliverables to domain KPIs (e.g. patient enrolment velocity, data lock timelines, regulatory submission accuracy)
Distinguish between effort-based and outcome-based success metrics, and explain why the latter matters more in Life Sciences client engagements

units.title: Using AI to Accelerate Delivery & Demonstrate Client Impact
learning_objectives: Apply GenAI tools to automate progress tracking, flag delivery risks, and generate stakeholder-ready status reports in a Life Sciences project context

Demonstrate how AI-assisted delivery practices translate into visible, measurable client impact — connecting technical outputs to business outcomes such as faster regulatory approval timelines or improved trial data quality
